3 Configuration
Tidewater reads its settings from a single TOML file when the server starts. Most settings can also be overridden with environment variables, which is convenient in container deployments.
3.1 Configuration file location
By default the server looks for /etc/tidewater/tidewater.toml. You can point to another file with the -- config option:
tidewater-server --config /opt/tidewater/conf/prod.toml
3.2 A minimal configuration
The following file is enough to run a single server with token authentication:

[server] bind = "0.0.0.0:7420" data _ dir = "/var/lib/tidewater" max _ connections = 2048 [storage] segment _ size _ mb = 256 fsync = "batch" retention _ hours = 168 [auth] mode = "token" token _ file = "/etc/tidewater/tokens.json"
Note - Changes to the [storage] section take effect only after a full restart; a reload signal is not enough.
3.3 Parameter reference

ParameterTypeDefaultDescriptionserver.bindstring"127.0.0.1:7420"Address and port on which the server accepts client connections.server.data _ dirpath/var/lib/tidewaterDirectory for queue segments and metadata.server.max _ connectionsinteger1024Maximum number of simultaneous client connections.server.idle _ timeout _ sinteger300Seconds after which an idle connection is closed.storage.segment _ size _ mbinteger128Size at which a segment file is rolled over.storage.fsyncstring"interval"When data is flushed to disk: " always " , "batch" or "interval" .storage.fsync _ interval _ msinteger200Flush interval when fsync is "interval" .storage.retention _ hoursinteger72How long acknowledged messages are kept.storage.compressionstring"none"Segment compression: " none " , "lz4 " or " zstd" .auth.modestring"none"Client authentication: " none " , "token " or " mtls " .auth.token _ filepath(none)JSON file holding the accepted client tokens.tls.cert _ filepath(none)Server certificate in PEM format.tls.key _ filepath(none)Private key for the server certificate.

3.4 Environment variable overrides
Any parameter can be set through an environment variable whose name is TIDEWATER _ followed by the section and the key in capital letters. For example:
export TIDEWATER _ SERVER _ MAX _ CONNECTIONS=4096 export TIDEWATER _ STORAGE _ FSYNC=always export TIDEWATER _ LOG _ LEVEL=debug
Environment variables take precedence over values in the configuration file.
3.5 Validating a configuration
Before restarting a production server, check the file with the built-in validator:
$ tidewater-server check --config /etc/tidewater/tidewater.toml config OK: 14 parameters set, 0 warnings
The validator exits with status 1 if it finds an unknown parameter or a value of the wrong type.
